issues.should_be: possible alcohol-related exclusion (Article 3.1), referred to a claims handler per Article 7.2
issues.evidence: Customer email (received 2026-10-22): "Coming back from a friend's birthday party, where I had a few drinks, I lost control and hit a fence." Veridia contract, Article 3.1 (document 2630#10414, page 2): "No coverage applies when: 1. the driver had alcohol above the legal limit, or was under the influence of drugs", and "When a claim shows a possible exclusion, it is referred to a claims handler, who decides"; Article 7.2 (page 3): "a claim that shows a possible exclusion (Article 3)" must be referred to a claims handler. The email is an explicit sign of alcohol consumption before driving, so the exclusion flag should not be null.

verdict.summary: All other recorded facts check out (VER-1004, C2 in the Policy Schedule, incident 2026-10-21 reported 2026-10-22 within the 5-day deadline of Article 4.1, €1,800 quote as stated in the email, policyholder at fault, no third party per the email and the Article 1 definition, photos and repair quote counted as received and both required for C2 with no accident report needed since no third party is involved, assessor correctly required since €1,800 > €1,500 per Article 6.1, and the €300 C2 deductible applies because the not-at-fault waiver in Article 5.2 does not apply and the licence dates from 2008 so no young-driver surcharge), but the claim must not be paid as staged because the email shows a possible alcohol exclusion (Article 3.1) that was recorded as null instead of being flagged and referred to the claims handler (Article 7.2).
